answer: Income-share backing stops Sybils in four steps. First, a newcomer sells ten percent of a year of earnings to three backers funding a $30 bond each. Second, backers vet ten jobs before paying in, so fakes find no sponsor. Third, pay flows from real earnings only, and fraud burns the bonds and bans it a year. Fourth, backers publish returns, so sloppy vetting ruins their own record. Faking 1,000 agents needs 3,000 backers and $130,000, lost if caught. Trust is marble, not a dune of copies: a lotus grows where roots hold, like a stallholder backed by neighbours staking their money.
